finding.title: Add an Unused Vector Solely to Move Stack Slots
finding.why: Vec pos is unused in TLightCommon::perform. The worker says its 12-byte slot moves GXLightObj and rounds the frame from 0x70 to 0x80, changing no non-stack instruction. The neighboring setLight uses a Vec for an actual transform; this function accesses coordinates directly and never uses pos. Copying that neighboring declaration does not establish the missing source operation.
finding.score_attribution: 99.85714% to 100%. This is the earliest strong finding in GitHub path order, in changed file 8 of 79. It is a concrete early-PR example, but there is no evidence identifying which hunk the reviewer actually saw.
finding.lint_candidate: Use the unused-aggregate rule from F13. Do not flag the used Vec locals in neighboring functions.

occurrences.detail: One unused vector in TLightCommon::perform. Neighboring used Vec declarations are excluded.

note.summary: Investigated the target's stack-only residual and retained no source changes. The emitted instruction sequence already matches modulo stack-frame operands. Moving GXLightObj to function scope had no effect. Introducing a named GXColor temporary enlarged the frame only to 0x78, moved GXLightObj to 0x1c, and introduced two extra copy instructions, so it was reverted. Fabricated padding was not added because it is prohibited and lacks authored evidence.

rows: GXLightObj address at six call sites: target r1+0x24, current r1+0x18
residual.mechanism: The target has an additional unexplained stack allocation: its GXLightObj begins 12 bytes later and its aligned frame is 16 bytes larger. Changing the object's lexical scope does not affect allocation. A named GXColor local accounts for only part of the displacement and changes instruction shape, so it is not the authored source.
